first_text_paint.limitation: Existing probe does not establish physical paint or isolate React rendering latency.

turn_trace_first_visible.limitation: Database NOW persistence anchor; not precise upstream or browser frame timestamp.

first_visible.interval_limitation: Prompt-to-first-thinking uses database persistence anchor and log wall time, so it is approximate; do not equate it to provider-only TTFT.

journal.limitation: Grok creates billing journal early; created_at is not upstream fetch start.

route_context.limitation: Mutable last_used_at is not first relay/fetch time. Expired state observed after successful terminal is consistent with turn cleanup, not proof of route failure.

safe_negative_evidence.limitation: Absence of this warning does not prove absence of all internal provider retry or queue behavior.

conclusions: Master accepted the turn within 0.633s of admission and prompt construction completed 1.573s after inbound. The 40s delay was not explained by gateway submit locks, memory barrier, or prompt assembly.

The long unpartitioned segment is after prompt construction and before first thinking, covering Grok CLI startup/catalog/auth/relay/provider queue and model behavior. Existing live markers cannot separate these components.
First thinking-to-first-text adds 18.868s on the same server milestone clock. This is stream behavior before the frontend renders正文.
The completed n=1 candidate-frontend observation is not a controlled causal comparison with the earlier 13.7s baseline. No frontend regression or supplier-only bottleneck is established.
